assets.name: Spoon-billed sandpiper
assets.source_pixel_provenance: Detailed head/body pixels are retained from the first pose of the new generated motion sheet. The generated leg phases were replaced by a deliberately authored two-leg contact/recovery plan and native branched-toe corrections; the original rounded pale belly rim is retained.
assets.native_edit_summary: New reference and generated motion draft. Retained russet head, spatulate bill, white belly and patterned wings. Stabilized head/body across the row boundary. Repainted two lower legs and toes with opposite phases, fixed y=109 ground, bent recovery toes and connected ankles. No pecking mixed into walking.
review_observations: The complete spatulate bill, short-necked russet head, patterned wings and pale rounded belly remain recognizable.
The two legs exchange forward/backward support and flexed recovery in the actual eight native poses; cross-row head/body jumping is removed.
The initially triangular feet were rejected and corrected natively. The final6x ankle/toe view shows thin toe branches separated by transparent pixels, with folded recovery toes.
All eight native poses and the decoded GIF sequence, including7→0, were reviewed separately from file-integrity checks.

native_limb_articulation.note: Articulation parameters guide native canvas edits; actual saved-layer alpha, contours and visible contacts were separately inspected. They do not by themselves prove good motion.

residual_limits: This is a stylized walking showcase, not a certified scientific feline gait model.
Head, torso and tail stay calm while the four limbs articulate; the artwork does not animate full muscle or fur dynamics.
Far hind paw is mostly occluded in poses0/1; native diagnostic silhouettes preserve its ownership and complete layer pixels.
The small reference-derived limb warp is finished with native contour edits; it is not a wholly hand-drawn blank-canvas animation.
No playable-game controller integration or animation blending has been implemented for this README sample.
